lines_of_business: Not stated beyond 'Blue Shield of California'; Benefit Application says contract language controls
effective_or_revised: Original Policy Date April 3, 2009; Effective Date July 1, 2026 (policy 2.01.18)
sections_in_order: Policy Guidelines (HSAT devices, contraindications, sleep lab test, definitions, risk factors, questionnaires, pediatric, bariatric, weight change, MSLT, specialist training, split-night, categorization)
criteria_location: Policy Statement I-IX on pp.1-2 (short roman-numeral statements); the real thresholds live in Policy Guidelines pp.2-7 (device sensor requirements, contraindications list, risk factors, clinically significant OSA). Statements refer to Policy Guidelines for terms.
procedures_covered: CPAP titration in lab (adult and pediatric)

logic.top_level: pathways: numbered statements I-IX each with letter sub-lists; mostly any-of

k_of_n.quote: individuals with any two of the following symptoms are considered to have a moderate-to-high probability for moderate to severe OSA: Habitual snoring; Observed apneas; Excessive daytime sleepiness; A body mass index (BMI) greater than 35 kg/m2

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: HSAT contraindications 'include, but are not limited to significant, ongoing symptoms related to' 10 conditions in Policy Guidelines; neuromuscular list in separate sub-list; statements III, VIII: repeat/unmet HSAT 'investigational'.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Statement I covers REPEAT HSAT (initial HSAT is required by guideline, no PA); IV initial PSG; VI repeat PSG; III repeat HSAT investigational when routine/sequential nights.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: may be considered medically necessary for an individual with a moderate or high pretest probability of OSA in any of the following situations
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'May be considered' is permissive; pretest probability defined only by 2-of-4 list in guidelines ('any two ... considered moderate-to-high').

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Prior authorization is not required for HSATs. However, treatment based on HSAT results will not be approved unless the following criteria are met
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Criteria apply to downstream treatment approval, not to HSAT itself; a checker for the HSAT request would have almost nothing to evaluate.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Contraindications to home sleep studies include, but are not limited to significant, ongoing symptoms related to
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Open list and 'significant, ongoing symptoms' vague.

extraction_hazards: Roman-numeral statements split across pages with the 'Blue Shield' footer in between; letter sub-lists continue after the break.
Policy Guidelines contain definitions that are not referenced by name in the statements.
The statement text says 'Repeat' for HSAT while the guideline requires HSAT first - the initial HSAT rule lives only in Policy Guidelines.
Appendix A and Regulatory Status table (SleepImage) are noise.
interesting_structures: Policy states HSAT is required first ('BSC requires an unattended ... HSAT as the initial study ... unless contraindicated') without prior-auth for HSAT.
Device specification rules (sensor sets, PAT) are part of coverage.
Coding corrections inside guidance (use G0400 for dual-belt devices).

fit_to_tree.why: Statements are simple any-of lists, but key definitions are in guidance prose, HSAT-first rule is outside the numbered statements, and probabilistic/clinical-judgment terms.
